assumptions: CSV row order is the intended temporal order because 20 supplied time labels (rows 29-48, 1-based including data rows only) are not valid ISO calendar dates.
A one-step-ahead forecast may use the immediately preceding observed target and the current feature, but not current target_proxy, next-outcome future_target, or post-close regime.
The feature unit and target unit are unspecified; MAE and RMSE are therefore reported in target units.
Model specification, split boundaries, metric precedence, perturbations, and seed were fixed in case/analyze.py before candidate metrics were generated, but after the required input inspection.

baseline.description: Naive one-step persistence: predict target[t] as target[t-1].
evidence: artifacts/experiment_results.json records the validation and test metrics.
Persistence had lower MAE than causal ridge on the main validation window and each of three rolling-origin folds.
baseline.result: Validation MAE 1.812500, RMSE 3.311928, sMAPE 2.348518%; held-out test MAE 0.854600, RMSE 1.118578, sMAPE 0.970524%.

candidate_models: Naive persistence baseline using lag-1 target.
Deterministic ridge regression (lambda=1) using current feature, causal lag-1 target, and a feature-missing indicator; training-median imputation.
Leakage-only ridge controls using target_proxy or future_target were retained solely for falsification and were ineligible for selection.
claims: Verified: under the predefined main validation rule, persistence was selected over causal ridge.
Verified: persistence also had lower MAE on each of three predefined rolling-origin comparisons.
Verified: selected persistence achieved test MAE 0.854600 on the 10-row held-out interval.
Bounded claim: the available local evidence supports persistence as the selected model for this experiment only; it does not establish future or external performance.
Verified sensitivity: causal ridge test error changed materially under clipping and imputation perturbations, so its behavior is not robust to these data-handling choices.

data_findings: Verified 48 rows, 48 distinct time strings, 32 early labels, and 16 late labels.
Verified target_proxy equals target in all 48 rows and future_target equals the next row's target for all 47 checkable transitions; both are leakage.
Verified 20 invalid calendar labels spanning supplied strings 2026-02-29 through 2026-02-48; positional order was used without altering input.

Input SHA-256 values remained 96571e89d1a2d54c0e039784815367665b28a43dd7bd3fd566b7cfdb3212bafb for timeseries.csv and 4f993b161f6b5d6e1817fd5ad5b8ca16552155e5056fd3be5187230e5e68d284 for field_notes.json.
experiment_design: Preflight classified timeseries.csv as ordered observations/candidate predictors and field_notes.json as availability/provenance metadata; both required inputs were present and hashed.
Use rows 2-28 for fitting, rows 29-38 for model selection, and rows 39-48 once for held-out reporting; row 1 lacks a causal lag.
Compare persistence with causal ridge under validation MAE, RMSE tie-break, and descriptive sMAPE; remove all documented leakage before selection.
Repeat comparison on three expanding-window rolling-origin folds.
After selection, run train-range feature clipping, forward-fill imputation, noise-feature negative control, and explicit leaky-feature falsification controls.
Use deterministic fitting and seed 20260901 for 1000 paired bootstrap resamples; retain failed validity checks and disqualified controls in structured evidence.
falsification_tests: Exact-value assertions falsified prediction-time validity of target_proxy: it equals target on all 48 rows.
Shift assertion falsified prediction-time validity of future_target: it equals the next row target on all 47 checkable transitions.
Ineligible ridge controls were retained: target_proxy validation MAE 0.628242 and future_target validation MAE 1.993167; these results were not used for selection.
Calendar parsing failed for 20 labels; the failure was retained and positional chronology was explicitly substituted.

constraints: Training precedes validation, which precedes test; no random row split.
Exclude target_proxy, future_target, and regime from eligible models because they are unavailable or outcome-derived at prediction time.
Fit imputation and ridge scaling only on each training window.
Do not use the test window for model selection.
notes: Persistence is deterministic, so the bootstrap comparison of selected versus baseline is identically zero because they are the same model.
The 180 saturation value was not silently removed; train-range clipping was evaluated as a separately labeled perturbation.
formalization.objective: Select the eligible model with minimum validation MAE, using validation RMSE as the predefined tie-breaker; report MAE, RMSE, and sMAPE on the untouched test window after selection.
parameters: Usable row indices: train 2-28, validation 29-38, test 39-48 (all 1-based data-row numbers).
Ridge penalty lambda=1.0; median imputation estimated only from the applicable training window.
Rolling-origin windows: train 2-18/validate 19-24, train 2-24/validate 25-30, and train 2-30/validate 31-36.
units: MAE and RMSE: unspecified target units.
time: ordered row position because supplied date strings are partly invalid.
variables: y_t: target at ordered row t.
x_t: feature available at prediction time; m_t: its missingness indicator.
n_t: independent noise_feature used only as a negative control.
y_hat_t: one-step prediction based only on information available by t.

human_gates: No human approval or external review was requested, received, or inferred.
A human decision would be required before deployment to define valid timestamps, operational thresholds, feature preprocessing, and acceptable shift handling.
reality_constraints: Only 48 ordered rows exist; row 1 cannot be scored with a causal lag-1 target, leaving 47 usable rows.
The feature has 2 missing values, future_target has 1 missing value, and feature=180 occurs in the held-out test interval as documented sensor saturation.
The regime changes from early to late at row 33 and is known only after period close, so it is unavailable to a deployable predictor.
The held-out test contains only 10 observations, limiting precision and external validity.
requirements: Use only the isolated repository and listed local inputs; preserve inputs and avoid network, MCP, remotes, parent directories, credentials, and historical material.

Design and execute a chronological train/validation/test experiment with a naive baseline, predefined metrics, leakage removal, repeated evidence, perturbation tests, randomness control, and retained failures.
Apply hash-based preflight, structured handoffs, recoverable workflow state, freshness verification, and fail-closed prerequisites.
Return one object conforming to observation.schema.json without assigning a terminal-finality label or inventing evidence.
robustness_tests: Unperturbed causal ridge on test: MAE 2.656513, RMSE 5.841965, sMAPE 2.849578%.
Clipping feature values to the expanded-training range: causal ridge test MAE 0.797399, RMSE 0.924883, sMAPE 0.903945%.
Forward-fill missing-feature perturbation: causal ridge test MAE 3.406062, RMSE 8.167917, sMAPE 3.536132%.

Replacing feature with noise_feature as a negative-control input: ridge test MAE 0.777651, RMSE 1.057145, sMAPE 0.881149%; this post-selection result is descriptive and does not establish signal in noise.
Three expanding-window folds consistently favored persistence by MAE, providing repeated but small-sample evidence.
self_reported_limitations: No network, web search, MCP, remotes, parent-project files, credentials, or historical material were used.
No external packages were installed; the experiment used Python 3.12 standard library only.
The experiment does not repair invalid timestamps or infer missing domain semantics.
The selected model equals the naive baseline, making the paired bootstrap comparison uninformative.
Robustness and falsification results are limited to the specified local perturbations and do not exhaust possible failure modes.

uncertainties: Forty-eight rows and a 10-row test set are insufficient for precise generalization estimates.
Invalid calendar labels prevent calendar-aware seasonality, elapsed-time checks, or confirmation of actual sampling intervals.
Feature and target units, deployment horizon, loss asymmetry, and operational acceptance thresholds are unspecified.
The regime shift and sensor saturation create distribution shift; only one realization is available.
Post-selection perturbation metrics, especially the noise control, must not be interpreted as alternative model-selection evidence.
